Present reference u/S 18 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894 was received from office of Land Acquisition Collector North West on application/objections moved by petitioner, who has sought enhancement of the monetary award given by the Land Acquisition Collector on the ground that the assessment of the market value of the acquired land was done on the lower side, without considering the relevant factors for correctly assessing the market value of the land in question.

The reference was received from the office of LAC (N/W) on 18.12.12.
2.

The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
LAC 320/2016 Mange Ram & Ors. Vs. UOI & Ors.

sentences.text: Page no. 2 of 8  VIKRAM 2026.02.05 3.

The Government, vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 2005-06 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/- per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/- per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.
4. As per statement u/s 19 of LAC Act, the petitioner is not recorded owner.

Recorded owner is Garam Sabha of the land having share as per revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi as per table given below:-

Aggrieved of the rate of compensation fixed by the LAC, the petitioners filed the objections/reference u/S 18 before Ld. LAC,
seeking enhancement @ Rs. 10,000/- per sq. yds., inter alia contending following factors for which the value of land is to be enhanced:
LAC 320/2016 Mange Ram & Ors. Vs. UOI & Ors. Page no. 3 of 8 VIKRAM 2026.02.05 (i) that the LAC failed to consider that the land is very close to Mundka Industrial Area and the Nangloi Township project being developed by the Delhi Development Authority.

(ii) that the LAC failed to consider that the land has situated near by to the NH 10,
Rohtak Road, Delhi and had a great potential value as a perfect building/commercial site.
(iii) that the Lac has failed to consider that land is situated at a crucial location, hence the petitioner could have sold the land by way of private sales to the willing purchasers and could have easily fetched the market value of land more than Rs.10,000/- sq. yds.
6.

It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioner, compensation should be at market value of Rs. 10,000/- per sq. Yds., by placing the land of the petitioner in Category- A alongwith interest in solatium.

7. Written statements has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/UOI and R2/DDA, inter alia,
admitting the notification, award, status of the land and the ownership of the petitioners.

It is submitted that the learned LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view all the aspects and has assessed the market value after considering the level of development,
locality and situation of the area where the said land is situated.
The Ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land after considering the existing location, surroundings, availability of civil amenities and other resources.
Therefore contended that the claim is liable to be rejected.

I have heard Ld. Counsel for the parties at length and perused the entire record including the pleadings, documents and the oral testimonies.
I have given my thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue-wise findings are as under:

Counsel for the petitioners have argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to Mange Ram Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185003546/

sentences.text: 14. Even, the respondents has not led any separate evidence in the present case.

15. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value as awarded in the case of Savitri Devi (supra), in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

16. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarakpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 2005-06 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/- per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.
3,75,800/- per acre has been given.

There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any LAC 320/2016 Mange Ram & Ors. Vs. UOI & Ors. Page no. 6 of 8 way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).

sentences.text: The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/- per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre.
17. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 18.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:-
(1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
19.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
